Name: Name
showTabBarDescription: Controls whether the tab bar is visible or not
tabBarPositionDescription: Controls where the tab bar is positioned
promptWhenClosingTabDescription: When enabled, you will be prompted when you close a tab
launchMinimizedDescription: When enabled, the app will start minimized
launchToTrayDescription: When Altus + starts with Windows, it stays in the tray without opening the window. Accounts connect and notify as usual. Needs the tray icon.
rememberWindowSizeDescription: When enabled, Altus will remember the size of the window from previous use
rememberWindowPositionDescription: When enabled, Altus will remember the position of the window from previous use
preventEnterDescription: When enabled, pressing Enter while typing adds a new line instead of sending the message. Ctrl+Enter sends it.
sendWithRightShiftEnterDescription: When enabled, Right Shift + Enter sends the message. Left Shift + Enter still adds a new line.
customTitlebarDescription: When enabled, Altus will use a custom titlebar instead of the one provided by the system. (NOTE: Requires a restart for changes to apply.)
autoHideMenuBarDescription: When enabled, the menu bar will only show when you press the Alt key
trayIconDescription: Controls whether the tray icon is visible or not
registerProtocolDescription: If enabled, Altus will register itself as the default handler for whatsapp:// links. (NOTE: Requires a restart for changes to apply.)
closeToTrayDescription: When enabled, Altus will be minimized to the tray instead of being closed completely
exitPromptDescription: When enabled, you will be prompted when you close the app
autoLaunchDescription: When enabled, Altus will launch whenever you start your system.
showSaveDialogDescription: Whether to ask where to save each file before downloading. (NOTE: Requires a restart for changes to apply.)
defaultDownloadDirDescription: The directory where you want to save the downloads. (NOTE: Requires an absolute path)
deleteThemeConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this theme?
Are you sure you want to exit?: Are you sure you want to exit?
Mute notifications until turned back on: Mute notifications until turned back on
resourceTestDescription: Altus + restarts and records the CPU and memory of every account from startup: once a second for the first 5 minutes, then every 10 seconds.
resourceTestUsage: Accounts, notifications and sound work as usual meanwhile. The results stay on this computer, in the resource-tests folder of the Altus + profile; the last 10 tests are kept.
resourceTestEnd: To finish, choose Help → End Resource Test: the folder opens with the results and Altus + restarts normally. Quitting Altus + also ends the test.
resourceTestSummaryComputer: Computer: {cpus} logical CPUs, {ram} GB of RAM
resourceTestSummaryStartupTimes: Times since Windows created the process: Node.js {node} s, Altus + code {script} s, Electron ready {ready} s, window created {window} s
resourceTestSummaryStartupTimesFromNode: Times since Node.js started: Altus + code {script} s, Electron ready {ready} s, window created {window} s
resourceTestSummaryPeak: Peak in the first 5 minutes: CPU {cpu} % after {cpuAt} s, memory {memory} MB after {memoryAt} s
resourceTestSummaryCalm: CPU calm (below 2 % for 15 s) after {seconds} s
resourceTestSummaryNotCalm: The CPU never stayed below 2 % for 15 s
resourceTestSummaryAccount: {name}: {start} MB after startup, {end} MB at the end, highest {max} MB
resourceTestSummaryMain: {start} MB after startup, {end} MB at the end, highest {max} MB
resourceTestSummaryMainJs: of which JavaScript: {start} MB after startup, {end} MB at the end (lowest value over 10 minutes)
resourceTestSummaryTooShort: Growth over time needs a test of at least 30 minutes after startup.
resourceTestSummaryTotal: Total at the end: {memory} MB, CPU {cpu} %
resourceUsageNote: Memory is each process's private memory, which Task Manager's Memory column counts differently. CPU is the share of the whole computer, as in Task Manager. Updated every 2 seconds while this window is open.
